conclusion: No blocking unsafe-code or allocation-contract finding in root review.
checks: A successful Acquire CAS creates the unique guard; failed acquisition neither blocks nor allocates.
Guard Drop publishes value writes with Release before the next acquisition.
UnsafeCell references are bounded by guard borrow lifetimes; DerefMut requires exclusive guard access.
TryLock Sync requires T Send; automatic guard traits additionally see PhantomData<&mutT>, requiring T Sync to share a guard.
Moving a guard across threads is sound for the atomic lock, which has no pthread owner-thread requirement.
Forgetting a guard only leaves the lock unavailable; no safe access bypass remains.
No OS mutex, allocator operation, wait, or destructor callback is introduced by lock/guard mechanics.
test_review: Value destroyed exactly once when owner drops
Selected allocator failure leaves value intact and permits reacquisition
Compile-fail guardSync check for Cell payload
scope: Value channel integration and caller callback lifetimes also require combined tests/fuzzing; the primitive itself does not establish those semantics.
